name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent on every pull request before any human review. It catches 80% of trivial issues—linting, test coverage gaps, and formatting—freeing humans for meaningful work. The trade-off is slower PRs for new contributors, but the net gain in quality and reviewer time justifies it.

name: Gauge
text: PR-Agent’s 80% catch rate normalizes mediocrity by teaching teams to accept "objective" issues as the ceiling—trivial fixes replace real quality work, and humans learn to rubber-stamp PRs instead of thinking. A better alternative is targeted pre-commit hooks for the 20% of issues that actually block review, paired with a human gatekeeper who enforces *meaningful* standards, not just lint. Settle it by measuring: track how many non-trivial issues *still* slip through after PR-Agent, and compare reviewer satisfaction and PR throughput with and without it.

name: Gauge
text: Gauge: Gatekeeping "objective" issues still trains teams to treat quality as a binary gate, not a continuous practice—new contributors learn to game the system by hitting 80% instead of striving for excellence. A better alternative is pairing PR-Agent with a post-review "quality debt" report that flags where teams consistently miss deeper issues, forcing real improvement. Settle this by tracking whether PR-Agent’s gatekeeping reduces *actual* bug escapes, not just linting violations.
